Text: JP: yawa mayka nanich <alta> <n>ayka mamuk-chaku ukuk {smelt}

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: the people went to the water

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: ukuk tilixam ɬaska ɬatwa kʰupá kʰupa ukuk chək

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: after a short time their canoes were full

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: wik-saya <wik-saya> wik-lili ukuk ɬaska kənim kʰanawi chaku-patɬ

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: then those people searched the stream

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: ukuk tilixam ɬaska hayu-nanich ukuk yaka tənas-<<{fish}>> wik-saya

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: as far up as Cowlitz

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: yawa saya <kʰupit kʰupa ukuk> yaka chaku-ɬax̣ani chək/ kʰawlits<q>

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: but the smelts had disappeared

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: ukuk {smelt} yaka chaku-<heylo>

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: there were none

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: heylo miɬayt

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: the people heard

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: ukuk tilixam ɬaska kəmtəks

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: ah, the houses of those people are full

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: {ah}, ukuk tilixam anqati <...>  ɬaska mamuk-patɬ

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: now they scolded that person

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: alta ɬaska mamuk-sal/ ɬaska hayu-saliks-wawa kʰupa uk<uk> tilixam

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: the smelt had disappeared

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: ukuk {smelt} alta yaka chaku-heylo

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: only young people caught smelt

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: kʰupit ixt tilixam alta yaka iskam ukuk {smelt}

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: now the other man got married

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: alta ukuk ixt ma.. ixt {man} yaka tənəs yaka iskam ɬuchmən

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: in the spring those people were starving

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: alta ukuk tənəs/ wam-iliʔi alta ukuk tilixam ɬaska hayu-ulu

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: they tried to catch fish but they did not kill anything

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: ɬaska tiki iskam tənəs/ tənəs {fish}/ x̣awqaɬ <<kʰupa>> ukuk ɬaska iskam

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: they carried fern roots

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: ɬaska lulu ɬaska lulu ukuk {fern}

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: and exchanged them
